statement: Street trees lower heat-stress emergency department visits in New York City through lower neighbourhood temperature: the composed path trees -> surface temperature -> heat ED rate is negative across community districts.

graph_evidence.relationship_id: (concepts I2CN3brExA tree, lHLIKbfnYp green space, RF7tCwCaa5 vegetation cover)
graph_evidence.summary: The tree concept has no relationships. Green space has 14, none with temperature, heat illness or emergency care. Surface temperature links only to air temperature (r about 0.9, 2 studies), population density (r 0.82) and deforestation (r 0.89). No finding connects trees or green space to heat-related ED visits.

Hasan et al. 2022 (Mymensingh, Bangladesh, Landsat 1988-2016): strong negative correlation of land surface temperature with NDVI. The graph stores r = -1.0, which is not the reported value (the abstract gives no number). The only vegetation-temperature finding found.

Sun et al. 2021 (BMJ, 74 million insured US adults, 2010-2019): days at the local 95th percentile of warm-season temperature had 66.3% (60.2 to 72.7) excess risk of ED visits for heat-related illness, with stronger effects in the Northeast. Stowell et al. 2023 (US children): OR 1.34 (1.16 to 1.56), ages 6-12.
Satellite surface temperature tracks ground air temperature (r about 0.9; R2 0.9).

literature.citation: Madrigano J, Ito K, Johnson S, Kinney PL, Matte T. A case-only study of vulnerability to heat wave-related mortality in New York City (2000-2011). Environ Health Perspect 2015;123:672-678.
literature.finding: Heat-wave deaths in NYC were more likely among Black residents and in areas with less green space and higher surface temperature (case-only design).

literature.citation: Ziter CD, Pedersen EJ, Kucharik CJ, Turner MG. Scale-dependent interactions between tree canopy cover and impervious surfaces reduce daytime urban heat during summer. PNAS 2019;116:7575-7580.
literature.finding: Bicycle-transect air temperatures in Madison: daytime air temperature falls with canopy cover, nonlinearly, with the largest cooling above about 40% canopy at 60-90 m scales.

literature.citation: Sun S et al. Ambient heat and risks of emergency department visits among adults in the United States. BMJ 2021;375:e065653.
literature.finding: 95th vs median warm-season temperature (34.4 C vs 14.9 C national average): heat-related illness ED visits +66.3% (60.2 to 72.7).

literature.citation: NYC DOHMH Environment and Health Data Portal, Heat Vulnerability Index (NTA); and EHDP-data repository, key-topics/heat-vulnerability-index.
literature.finding: The HVI is built from surface temperature, green space, household air conditioning, poverty or median income and percent Black residents, chosen because they predicted heat-related deaths. Using the HVI as an outcome of trees would be circular.

prediction.magnitude: Indirect effect (a*b, both adjusted for poverty and percent Black; b also for AC and trees) between -0.5% and -5% in the heat ED rate per 1 SD of log street-tree density. The total association of trees with the ED rate, unadjusted, may have either sign, because tree density and poverty are correlated across CDs; the adjusted indirect path is the registered quantity.
prediction.support_if: verdict 'bridged' if links heat-trees-surftemp and heat-surftemp-ed are each confirmed or unsettled with the right sign, and the bootstrap 95% interval of a*b lies below 0
prediction.refute_if: a*b positive with the bootstrap interval above 0, or either link contested

plan: Compose the two community-district links: a = adjusted slope of surface temperature on z(log trees/km2) (heat-trees-surftemp), b = adjusted slope of log heat ED rate on surface temperature, also adjusted for z(log trees/km2) (heat-surftemp-ed); indirect effect a*b with a nonparametric bootstrap over CDs (5,000 draws). Report also the total association of log ED rate on trees, unadjusted and adjusted. The hyperlocal within-NTA link (heat-trees-airtemp-hyperlocal) is reported beside the chain as the street-level check on link a. State which confounders the chain cannot separate (income, race, housing age and AC, building density) and what design would settle it.
alternatives: Income and race drive tree cover (historic planting and redlining), surface temperature and ED use together; 59 areal units cannot separate them
Ecological fallacy: area associations need not hold for individuals
Street trees are a small part of canopy; parks and backyard trees are omitted
Reverse placement: MillionTreesNYC targeted low-canopy, high-HVI neighbourhoods after 2007, so planting follows vulnerability
